oliver: Quick recap from the perf sync — we hit a couple of interacting problems: allocator fragmentation after the kernel rewrite + larger batch packing causing prefix-cache churn. proposing an adaptive per-shard priority (recency * token_count_factor) for evictions, not pure LRU.

jia: Sounds promising. worried about compute cost if we update priority on every access. can we approximate with exponential decay counters?

mike: +1 to decay counters. also we should add a backpressure hook into the runtime so when allocation fails we throttle batching before we OOM. today it just hard-ooms.

sara: I ran a quick smoke on dev-gpu-6 with 8k tokens median seq. baseline (master kernel) vs kernel-optimized weave:
```
# run config
--cache-shards=64 --ws-pool=128MB --batch-max=64
master: cache_hitrate=0.74, avg_shard=198kB, OOMs=0, alloc_failures=2
weave-kernel: cache_hitrate=0.70, avg_shard=215kB, OOMs=1, alloc_failures=9
```
We see hitrate drop and more alloc failures after the kernel change. suggests increased internal fragmentation.

oliver: That matches profiler flamegraphs — more small allocations and fewer large contiguous buffers. Two levers: (A) allocator reuse aggregator (coalesce small frees into workspace reuse list) (B) make prefix cache eviction prefer high-length prefixes to maximize token-saved/hit.

mike: For (A) I sketched a tiny change to the allocator: when a workspace is freed, push into a per-size-bucket freelist and prefer exact-size reuse before splitting new slabs. Also expose ENV var FAST_WS_REUSE=1 for testing. pseudocode:
```
if (free_size <= MAX_WS) freelist[bucket(free_size)].push(ptr)
on_alloc(req) {
  bucket = bucket(req.size)
  if (!freelist[bucket].empty()) return freelist[bucket].pop()
  else fallback_alloc()
}
```
This avoids small repeated mmap/alloc overhead and reduces fragmentation spikes.

jia: Nice. We should also track ws_reuse_hits in metrics so we can correlate with alloc_failures. add metric name: runtime.ws_reuse.hits.

sara: I'll run the A/B: three conditions on dev-gpu-8 for 2 hours each:
- baseline (master)
- allocator-reuse (FAST_WS_REUSE=1)
- adaptive-priority-evict (weight = recency + alpha * token_length)
I'll capture: eviction_count, avg_shard_bytes, cache_hitrate, ws_reuse_hits, allocation_failures, batch_latency_p95.

infra-bot: Job perf-ab-test-1938 started on dev-gpu-8. logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1938

oliver: One more note — batching heuristics change after the kernel patch increased average batch size because some kernels became cheaper, which pushed more KV cache insertions at peak. We should limit batch pack growth when cache pressure high. idea: batch controller reads a runtime signal `cache_pressure` (0-1) and reduces batch_max when >0.6.

mike: Implementation: add a sliding window estimator for cache_pressure = evictions / (evictions + hits) over last N accesses. If pressure > threshold, target_batch_max = max(8, base_batch_max * (1 - pressure)).

jia: Regression root-cause hypothesis: newer kernel reduces per-token compute but increases tiny allocations and accelerates cache churn -> more frequent evictions -> higher alloc failure probability. Tests above should confirm causal path.

sara: Running now. I'll post initial graphs in ~2h. if allocator-reuse reduces alloc_failures by >50% and recovers hitrate, we can ship `FAST_WS_REUSE` behind a feature flag.

oliver: Great. Also plan to add microtrace capture (prefix access sequence) for 5-minute window when alloc_failures spike so we can replay cache behavior offline. anyone want to own the trace parser?

mike: I'll take the parser. will sketch expected format and a small script to replay lookups + eviction decisions.

oliver: Perfect. thanks all — after sara posts the graphs we'll decide which patch to dogfood. :thumbsup:

sara: ack, will update thread when first run completes.

mike: ping me when trace is available, will start parser dev.

jia: thanks — I'll prepare a short perf test harness to sweep alpha in [0.1, 0.5, 1.0] for the weight calculation.

infra-bot: Job perf-ab-test-1938 completed (partial): alloc_failures reduced 62% in allocator-reuse run vs weave-kernel. full results pending.

oliver: Nice — preliminary green. we'll reconvene tomorrow to pick flags and rollout plan.
